hunks.baseline: “Well, look at this. This bastard’s got it made.”
hunks.sol: “Well, look at you. Must be nice.”

hunks.baseline: “Did you come here for a picnic? Sleeping in a Gate?”
hunks.sol: “Did you come here for a picnic? Who sleeps in the middle of a Gate?”

hunks.baseline: I must have dozed off. I answered, shameless.
hunks.sol: I must have dozed off. I shamelessly denied it.

hunks.baseline: “Tsk.”
hunks.sol: “Tch.”

hunks.baseline: He shook a fist at me, but a smile sat at the corners of his mouth. I rubbed my stiff neck.
hunks.sol: He shook a fist at me, but a smile tugged at the corners of his mouth. I rubbed my stiff neck.

hunks.baseline: “Did you meet a woman yesterday? Why are you nodding off like a sick chicken even in the middle of a raid?”
hunks.sol: “Did you meet a woman last night or something? Why are you nodding off like a sick chicken in the middle of a raid?”

hunks.baseline: We’d been through thick and thin for five years, from our first battle until now. He knew me as well as I knew him.
hunks.sol: We’d been through thick and thin together for five years, ever since our first battle. He knew me as well as I knew him.

hunks.baseline: His voice dropped low. I looked past his shoulder at the team members resting nearby and nodded.
hunks.sol: His voice dropped. I looked past his shoulder at the team members resting nearby and nodded.

hunks.baseline: “Well, well. This bastard gets a little time under his belt and now he’s stuffing his back pocket. And he’s the vice team leader, no less.”
hunks.sol: “Well, well. This bastard gets a little experience under his belt and starts lining his pockets on the side. And you call yourself the vice team leader.”

hunks.baseline: Hunters with professional licenses were legally barred from second jobs. Even a D-rank probably wouldn’t have to live like this, but F-ranks like us had no choice. That was why the Guild looked the other way even when they knew.
hunks.sol: Hunters with professional licenses were legally barred from taking second jobs. A D-rank Hunter probably wouldn’t have to live like this, but F-ranks like us had no choice. The Guild knew how things were, so they looked the other way even when they found out.

hunks.baseline: “True, but… be careful. If someone files a complaint with the Management Agency, it’ll become a real headache.”
hunks.sol: “True, but… be careful. If someone files a complaint with the Management Agency, you’ll have a real mess on your hands.”

hunks.baseline: “It’s a trustworthy place. They pay cash the same day, so there’s no problem. You think I’d do this for nothing?”
hunks.sol: “It’s a trustworthy place. They pay cash the same day, so there’s no problem. You think I’d risk it otherwise?”

hunks.baseline: Judging by his face, he was tempted.
hunks.sol: Judging by his expression, he was tempted.

hunks.baseline: “I’ve got three kids. I’d need an oil well to blow in the yard.”
hunks.sol: “I’ve got three kids. I need an oil well to spring up in my yard.”

hunks.baseline: He poured it out with a miserable look. I’d already heard this routine dozens of times. After venting about the misery of raising kids, the rising price of formula, and the shamelessness of merchants, he patted my shoulder.
hunks.sol: Misery filled his eyes as the words poured out. I’d already heard this routine dozens of times. After railing against the hardships of raising children, the rising price of formula, and the shamelessness of merchants, he patted me on the shoulder.

hunks.baseline: I had no woman and no money. My life’s goal was to buy a house in a safe zone within five years, so deep down I envied him.
hunks.sol: I had no woman and no money. My goal in life was to buy a house in a safe zone within five years, so deep down, I envied him.
A spouse I loved. Children. A happy family.

hunks.baseline: A spouse I loved, and kids. A happy family. I had no idea when I’d ever get something like that.
hunks.sol: I had no idea when I’d ever have something like that.

hunks.baseline: For all that talk, he had a reputation as a devoted husband and a good father. I knew how he sometimes took out his family photos and smiled fondly at them.
hunks.sol: For all his talk, he was famous for being a devoted husband and a good father. I knew he sometimes took out his family photos and smiled fondly at them.

hunks.baseline: “Your whole life gets sucked in. You come to your senses and you’re buried up to your chest, barely breathing.”
hunks.sol: “It sucks your whole life in. By the time you come to your senses, you’re buried up to your chest and can barely breathe.”

hunks.baseline: “So don’t just work. Take breaks. Dating, hobbies—stuff like that’s good for you.”
hunks.sol: “So don’t spend all your time working. Take breaks. Dating, hobbies—stuff like that’s good for you.”

hunks.baseline: I scratched my head as I answered. He looked at me with pity.
hunks.sol: I scratched my head as I answered. He gave me a concerned look.

hunks.baseline: “I saw you sleeping earlier, sweating cold the whole time. Keep that up and you’ll drop dead from overwork.”
hunks.sol: “I saw you sleeping earlier. You were drenched in cold sweat. Keep that up and you’ll drop dead from overwork.”

hunks.baseline: Now that he mentioned it, my back was damp with cold sweat. Must have been a bad dream…
hunks.sol: Now that he mentioned it, my back was damp with cold sweat. I must have had a bad dream….

hunks.baseline: These days it was how Hunters like me made a living, but its true nature was an invasion route for the Demon Realm’s army.
hunks.sol: These days, Gates provided a living for Hunters like me, but their true purpose was to serve as invasion routes for the armies of the Demon Realm.

hunks.baseline: When Demon King Asmodeus fell, his mighty army was routed with him. Decades later, the Gates were still there.
hunks.sol: When Demon King Asmodeus fell, his mighty army was routed with him. But even decades later, the Gates remained.

hunks.baseline: At his command, three Hunters bearing huge tower shields blocked the front. In a narrow cave, that alone was enough to soak most attacks.
hunks.sol: At his command, three Hunters carrying enormous tower shields blocked the path ahead. In a narrow cave, that alone was enough to stop most attacks.

hunks.baseline: About twenty goblins hurled poison needles, axes, and spears, but every one of them bounced off those big, beautiful tower shields.
hunks.sol: Some twenty goblins hurled poison needles, axes, and spears, but every last one bounced off those big, beautiful tower shields.

hunks.baseline: Up front, the tanks blocked every attack. From the rear, the archers poured arrows. We pushed forward and dropped about half of them, and the goblins let out panicked cries.
hunks.sol: The tanks blocked every attack from the front while the archers rained arrows from the rear. As we pressed forward and took down nearly half of them, the goblins let out panicked shrieks.

hunks.baseline: He timed the next order perfectly.
hunks.sol: He gave the next order at exactly the right moment.

hunks.baseline: The tanks dropped their tower shields and burst forward at the same time. I was faster.
hunks.sol: The tanks dropped their tower shields and charged.
I was faster.

hunks.baseline: I swung the iron spear in a wide arc. Green blood burst, and the front rank broke. I dove into the gap, stabbing and cutting at everything I could reach, and the line came crashing down.
hunks.sol: I swept the iron spear through a wide arc. Green blood burst into the air, and the front rank collapsed. I plunged into the gap, stabbing and slashing at everything within reach, and their formation crumbled.

hunks.baseline: The damage dealers and tanks piled in, and in an instant the goblin pack was a pile of corpses.
hunks.sol: The damage dealers and tanks piled in. In moments, the goblin pack had become a heap of corpses.

hunks.baseline: “Honestly, the vice team leader did half of it. He was flying around. When did he get that good…? Shh. The Team Leader’s pissed.”
hunks.sol: “Honestly, the vice team leader did half the work. He was flying around out there. When did he get that good…? Shh. The Team Leader’s pissed.”

hunks.baseline: The people chatting shut their mouths the moment he appeared.
hunks.sol: The team members chatting among themselves fell silent the moment he appeared.

hunks.baseline: That made me jump.
hunks.sol: That scared the hell out of me.

hunks.baseline: I’d been staring off, lost in thought, and I startled as I answered.
hunks.sol: I’d been staring into space, lost in thought, and jerked in surprise.

hunks.baseline: “Who told you to go solo? Are you a tank? Forget the attack order? And you still call yourself vice team leader?”
hunks.sol: “Who told you to go off on your own? Are you a tank? Did you forget the attack order? And you still call yourself the vice team leader?”

hunks.baseline: “If you’re going to act like this, transfer teams. You’re putting the rest of them in danger too.”
hunks.sol: “If you’re going to pull this kind of shit, transfer teams. You’re putting everyone else in danger.”

hunks.baseline: The feeling was strange. The moment I saw the goblin pack, I’d thought I could wipe them out by myself.
hunks.sol: It was a strange feeling. The instant I saw the goblin pack, I thought I could wipe them all out by myself.

hunks.baseline: No. That hadn’t been a thought.
hunks.sol: No, it hadn’t been a thought.

hunks.baseline: He swallowed the rest. We’d had each other’s backs for five years now, and this was the first time I’d ever pulled something like this.
hunks.sol: He swallowed whatever he had been about to say. We’d had each other’s backs for five years, and this was the first time I’d ever done anything so reckless.

hunks.baseline: “Don’t do it again. If you’re having a hard time, tell me.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t do it again. If something’s bothering you, tell me.”

hunks.baseline: I watched him walk away after patting my shoulder. For some reason, a spot in my chest throbbed.
hunks.sol: He patted my shoulder and walked away. As I watched him go, something in my chest throbbed.

hunks.baseline: But before long I wasn’t even thinking about the pain.
hunks.sol: But it wasn’t long before I stopped thinking about the pain altogether.

hunks.baseline: “Magic Gems!”
hunks.sol: “Magic Gem!”

hunks.baseline: “Got some!”
hunks.sol: “Got one here!”

hunks.baseline: “Jackpot! Jackpot! Jackpot!”
hunks.sol: “It dropped! It dropped! It dropped!”

hunks.baseline: Ah, that last shout was mine. His face was flushed too as he muttered.
hunks.sol: Ah, that last shout was mine.

hunks.baseline: “Hey, what is all this…?”
hunks.sol: His face was flushed with excitement too as he muttered, “What the hell is all this…?”

hunks.baseline: Twenty Magic Gems, large and small, lay neatly on the floor.
hunks.sol: Twenty Magic Gems of various sizes lay neatly arranged on the ground.

hunks.baseline: Magic Gems. They looked like red pebbles, but they were called the flower of the Gate. These lumps of mana that monsters carried were high-dimensional energy, and the most valuable byproduct a monster had.
hunks.sol: Magic Gems. They looked like red pebbles, but they were known as the flower of the Gate. These concentrations of mana found inside monsters were a form of higher-dimensional energy—and the most valuable of all monster byproducts.

hunks.baseline: “At this rate, each one’s got to be worth over a million won.”
hunks.sol: “At this size, each one has to be worth more than a million won.”

hunks.baseline: That from the Team Leader, an E-rank Hunter who’d lasted ten years in this business. People’s eyes went slack at the intoxicating sight.
hunks.sol: That came from the Team Leader, an E-rank Hunter who had survived ten years in this business. Everyone’s eyes went glassy at the intoxicating sight.

hunks.baseline: At the new recruit’s question, everyone shook their heads hard.
hunks.sol: At the new recruit’s question, everyone shook their heads emphatically.

hunks.baseline: In an F-rank Gate the average was one or two, and even with incredible luck you wouldn’t hit five.
hunks.sol: An F-rank Gate yielded one or two on average. Even with incredible luck, you wouldn’t find five.

hunks.baseline: *Twenty million from the Magic Gems alone, another five million for the byproducts and Equipment. Add all the various allowances and…*
hunks.sol: *At least twenty million from the Magic Gems alone. Another five million from the byproducts and Equipment. Add the various allowances on top of that, and…*

hunks.baseline: *Fuck. How much is this?*
hunks.sol: *Fuck. How much is all this?*

hunks.baseline: The biggest jackpot I’d hit since becoming a Hunter.
hunks.sol: It was the biggest jackpot I’d hit since becoming a Hunter.

hunks.baseline: “Almost there. Turn right and it’s the boss zone.”
hunks.sol: “We’re almost there. Turn right and the boss zone is just ahead.”

hunks.baseline: It went without saying, but a boss zone had a boss. A boss monster was the strongest monster in that Gate—and the one with the most expensive byproducts, Equipment, and Magic Gems.
hunks.sol: It went without saying, but a boss zone contained a boss. The boss monster was the strongest monster in the Gate—and the one with the most expensive byproducts, Equipment, and Magic Gems.

hunks.baseline: *If we take down the boss monster too?*
hunks.sol: *What if we take down the boss monster too?*

hunks.baseline: A literal jackpot. A once-in-a-lifetime chance for an F-rank Hunter.
hunks.sol: It would be a literal jackpot. The opportunity of a lifetime for an F-rank Hunter.

hunks.baseline: Everyone was smiling bright at the thought when he spoke.
hunks.sol: Everyone was beaming at the thought when he spoke.

hunks.baseline: What the hell was he talking about?
hunks.sol: What the hell was he saying?

hunks.baseline: “Think about it. Every monster we’ve run into has been an ordinary goblin. This many Magic Gems? Something’s off.”
hunks.sol: “Think about it. Every monster we’ve encountered has been an ordinary goblin, but we’ve found this many Magic Gems? Something’s wrong.”

hunks.baseline: He sighed. Excitement still hadn’t left his flushed face, but there was conflict on it too.
hunks.sol: He sighed. His face was still flushed with excitement, but now uncertainty clouded it.

hunks.baseline: “I know how you feel. I do… but we’ve already grabbed a fortune. Let’s be satisfied with this much and go back.”
hunks.sol: “I know how you feel. I do… but we’ve already made a fortune. Let’s be satisfied with this and turn back.”

hunks.baseline: Here? After coming this far, turn back?
hunks.sol: Now? After coming this far, he wanted to turn back?

hunks.baseline: I looked at the other team members. Some had been in sync for two or three years; some were new. They all had the same look I did.
hunks.sol: I looked at the other team members. Some of them had fought alongside me for two or three years. Others were new.
Every one of them wore the same expression I did.

hunks.baseline: I tried to keep talking, but no voice came out. Now there was ringing in my ears too.
hunks.sol: I tried to continue, but no sound came out. Now my ears had started ringing too.

hunks.baseline: The pain and the ringing got worse and worse. I dropped to my knees, gasping.
hunks.sol: The pain and the ringing grew worse. I dropped to my knees, gasping for breath.

hunks.baseline: I grabbed someone’s pant leg and hung on.
hunks.sol: I grabbed someone’s pant leg and clung to it.

hunks.baseline: It was him. The man who’d looked after me like a brother, like a father, for the past five years.
hunks.sol: It was him. The man who had looked after me like a brother—and like a father—for the past five years.

hunks.baseline: He looked down at me, indifferent.
hunks.sol: He looked down at me without emotion.

hunks.baseline: “Me? You, who ran and left everyone behind?”
hunks.sol: “Me? After you ran away and left everyone behind?”

hunks.baseline: I forgot the pain and stared at him. Clothes and skin melted away, and bone showed through. Everyone except me had become skeletons, sprawled across the ground.
hunks.sol: I forgot the pain and stared up at him. His clothes and skin melted away, exposing bone.
Everyone but me had become a skeleton sprawled across the ground.

hunks.baseline: They were all dead.
hunks.sol: They had all died.

hunks.baseline: That day two years ago. In the boss zone I had insisted we enter, they had all died.
hunks.sol: That day two years ago. In the boss zone I had insisted we enter, every one of them had died.
I floundered, drowning in the memories.

hunks.baseline: I floundered, buried in the memories. I remembered the ominous darkness that had settled over the boss zone, the foul smell, the damp floor, and that thing’s enormous wings.
hunks.sol: The ominous darkness hanging over the boss zone. The foul stench. The damp floor. That thing’s enormous wings.

hunks.baseline: Bodies ripped to shreds in midair. Screams of terror. People running.
hunks.sol: Bodies ripped to pieces in midair.
Terrified screams.
People running for their lives.

hunks.baseline: But even the Skill I had poured everything into hadn’t been enough to kill it. As I waited to die, he pulled me to my feet.
hunks.sol: But even the Skill I poured everything into wasn’t enough to kill it. As I waited for death, he hauled me to my feet.

hunks.baseline: If it hadn’t been for me. If I hadn’t gotten greedy, everyone could have lived. They could have gone home to their families.
hunks.sol: If it hadn’t been for me—if I hadn’t gotten greedy—everyone could have survived.
They could have gone home to their families.

hunks.baseline: I wailed like a child, and he forced a smile.
hunks.sol: As I sobbed like a child, he forced himself to smile.

hunks.baseline: *How is that your fault? Look at this kid, now you’re even playing Team Leader.*
hunks.sol: *How is that your fault? Look at this kid. Now you’re even trying to play Team Leader.*

hunks.baseline: The massive body drifted through the cave. Stalactites rained down, and the last member of the team let out a death cry. In the darkness, its red eyes turned toward us.
hunks.sol: The massive body floated through the cavern. Stalactites rained down, and the last member of the team screamed his final breath.
In the darkness, the monster’s red eyes turned toward us.

hunks.baseline: *That arrogant bastard. Taekyung, you go first.*
hunks.sol: *That arrogant bastard. Taekyung, go on ahead.*
My chest hurt.

hunks.baseline: My chest hurt. Pain rolled in hard enough to blank my vision. It felt like I had swallowed lava, like everything inside me was burning away. The ringing in my ears turned into a monster’s roar.
hunks.sol: Pain surged through me, fierce enough to blot out my vision. It felt as though I had swallowed lava, as though everything inside me was burning away.

hunks.sol: The ringing in my ears became a monster’s roar.

hunks.baseline: I woke with the scream.
hunks.sol: I woke with a scream.

hunks.baseline: But it wasn’t a Gate. There were no monsters, and no team members.
hunks.sol: But I wasn’t inside a Gate. There were no monsters and no team members.

hunks.baseline: Someone stood up at the window, where sunlight poured in.
hunks.sol: Someone rose from beside the window, where sunlight streamed into the room.

hunks.baseline: “Did you dream about my lord? He’ll be pleased if I tell him.”
hunks.sol: “Were you dreaming about my lord? He’ll be pleased when I tell him.”

hunks.baseline: Coldness dripped from his face.
hunks.sol: His face was as cold as ever.

hunks.baseline: Seeing him made it real that I was still inside the game.
hunks.sol: The sight of him drove home the fact that I was still inside the game.

hunks.baseline: “Then I’ll leave that part out of the report.”
hunks.sol: “Then I’ll leave that part out when I tell him.”

hunks.baseline: I was soaked in sweat. Through the gaps in the bandages wound tight around my whole body, I could see flesh raised with blood scabs.
hunks.sol: My entire body was drenched in sweat. Through the gaps between the bandages wrapped tightly around me, I could see skin crusted with scabs.

hunks.baseline: “You were unconscious for five days. Your condition was so critical that the Medicine King Hall Master concluded you wouldn’t last the day.”
hunks.sol: “You were unconscious for five days. Your condition was so critical that the Medicine King Hall Master concluded you wouldn’t survive another day.”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. When my lord heard that, he went berserk. If I hadn’t stopped him, he would have beaten the Medicine King Hall Master to death.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. When my lord heard, he flew into a rage. If I hadn’t stopped him, he would have beaten the Medicine King Hall Master to death.”

hunks.baseline: I remembered the old man from the meeting a few days ago, the one who had threatened to shove a giant needle into the White Tiger Hall Leader’s anus.
hunks.sol: I remembered the old man from the meeting a few days ago—the one who had threatened to drive a giant needle into the White Tiger Hall Leader’s anus.

hunks.baseline: *So he really had been chanting for me to die.*
hunks.sol: *So he’d practically been praying for me to die.*

hunks.baseline: “A great deal happened. Among it, there’s good news and even better news. Which would you like to hear first?”
hunks.sol: “A great deal. Among it all, there is good news and even better news. Which would you like to hear first?”

hunks.baseline: “First, the reconnaissance squad and the survivors of the Sakju Branch returned safely. Two of them suffered fairly serious injuries, but their lives are not in danger.”
hunks.sol: “First, the reconnaissance squad and the survivors of the Sakju Branch returned safely. Two of them suffered fairly serious injuries, but neither is in danger of dying.”

hunks.baseline: I remembered his face as he gasped out his last breath, a dagger in his throat and another between his brows. Twenty at most. Far too young to lose his life.
hunks.sol: I remembered his face as he gasped out his final breath, one dagger lodged in his throat and another between his brows.
He couldn’t have been more than twenty.
Far too young to die.

hunks.baseline: “Are you thinking of the dead?”
hunks.sol: “Are you thinking about the dead?”

hunks.baseline: “The body—did they recover the body?”
hunks.sol: “His body. Did you recover it?”

hunks.baseline: “We recovered it properly and buried him. He was an orphan with no one in the world, so there were no surviving relatives.”
hunks.sol: “We recovered and buried him properly. He was an orphan with no family in the world, so there were no relatives to notify.”

hunks.baseline: Wipeng didn’t wait for an answer. He took a step toward me and went on.
hunks.sol: Wipeng didn’t wait for my answer. He took a step toward me and continued.

hunks.baseline: “What does that…”
hunks.sol: “What do you mean…?”

hunks.baseline: “Martial artists are not beings meant to be protected. They are people who fight their enemies and prove themselves. He died facing an enemy too strong to do anything about, but that was not mere death—it was death in battle.”
hunks.sol: “Martial artists are not meant to be protected. They fight their enemies and prove themselves. He may have died facing an enemy too powerful for him to overcome, but his was not a meaningless death. He fell in battle.”

hunks.baseline: The idea that dying on a battlefield made it an honorable death was the biggest load of bullshit ever.
hunks.sol: The notion that dying on a battlefield somehow made it an honorable death was the biggest load of bullshit I had ever heard.
There was no such thing as an honorable death.

hunks.baseline: There was no such thing as an honorable death. Even now, the screams of my comrades who died two years ago and Number Seven’s wide-open eyes as his breath left him were still vivid.
hunks.sol: Even now, I could vividly hear the screams of my comrades who had died two years ago. I could still see Number Seven’s wide-open eyes as he breathed his last.

hunks.baseline: “The fact that he died hasn’t changed.”
hunks.sol: “The fact that he’s dead hasn’t changed.”

hunks.baseline: “There are people who cling to facts that will never change. I won’t say who.”
hunks.sol: “I have seen people obsess over facts that can never be changed. I won’t name anyone.”

hunks.baseline: “Then live his share as well.”
hunks.sol: “Then live enough for him as well.”

hunks.baseline: “I’m not telling you to forget the dead. Bury them in your heart and carve them into your mind. Use that regret as a foothold and soar to the place they dreamed of reaching. That is the path you must take, Young Master.”
hunks.sol: “I am not telling you to forget the dead. Bury them in your heart and carve them into your mind. Use that regret as your foothold, then soar to the place they dreamed of reaching. That is the path you must walk, Young Master.”

hunks.baseline: *The path I must take…*
hunks.sol: *The path I must walk…*

hunks.baseline: Just hearing those words made something in my chest lurch. I turned them over for a while, then let out a sudden laugh.
hunks.sol: The words alone made something stir deep in my chest. I thought them over for a while, then sagged back with a laugh.

hunks.baseline: “If I give it my whole life, can I make it there?”
hunks.sol: “If I devote my whole life to it, will I make it?”

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know. I don’t even know how far my own path goes, so how could I know yours?”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know. I don’t even know where my own path will end, so how could I know yours?”

hunks.baseline: “What’s at the end of the road Great Hero Wipeng is walking?”
hunks.sol: “What’s waiting at the end of your path, Great Hero Wipeng?”

hunks.baseline: A joke?
hunks.sol: Was he joking?

hunks.baseline: No. Wipeng was more serious and resolute than ever.
hunks.sol: No. Wipeng was more serious and resolute than I had ever seen him.

hunks.baseline: “Because it’s a dream.”
hunks.sol: “Because it is a dream.”

hunks.baseline: He was right. Dreams were always hard to reach.
hunks.sol: He was right. Dreams were always difficult to achieve.

hunks.baseline: Even more so if you were carrying the dreams of those you had lost.
hunks.sol: All the more so when you carried the dreams of those you had lost.

hunks.baseline: The moment Wipeng opened his lips, a cold winter wind shook the window.
hunks.sol: The moment Wipeng’s lips parted, a cold winter wind rattled the window.

hunks.baseline: Beyond the chill of the wind, I heard Number Seven’s name.
hunks.sol: Beyond the chill howl of the wind, I heard Number Seven’s name.

hunks.baseline: “That’s a cool name.”
hunks.sol: “That’s a great name.”

hunks.baseline: “I heard he chose it himself. His dream was just as big.”
hunks.sol: “I heard he chose it himself. His dream was every bit as grand.”

hunks.baseline: “The greatest of all time.”
hunks.sol: “To become the greatest of all time.”

hunks.baseline: “You’re going to have a hard time.”
hunks.sol: “You’ve got your work cut out for you.”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah. That’s unbelievable.”
hunks.sol: “Tell me about it. That’s ridiculous.”

hunks.baseline: A laugh slipped out. Only then did I feel the weight in my heart lift.
hunks.sol: A laugh escaped me. Only then did I feel the weight in my heart lift.

hunks.baseline: Wipeng tipped his head and spoke.
hunks.sol: Wipeng inclined his head and continued.

hunks.baseline: “Now, there’s still the even better news.”
hunks.sol: “Now, there is still the even better news.”

hunks.baseline: I waited, as expectant as I could get, for what he would say next.
hunks.sol: I waited eagerly to hear what he would say next.
